plan.summary: The owner of a team gets a 'Delete team' option in the team settings. After they confirm, the team and its memberships are removed, and anyone who was using that team is moved back to their personal team.
acceptance_criteria: A team owner can delete a non-personal team by sending DELETE to the route named teams.destroy with the team as the parameter, and is redirected with a success message.
After deletion the team and all of its memberships no longer exist in the database.
Every user whose current team was the deleted team, including the owner, has their current team switched to their personal team.
Admins of the team cannot delete it and receive a 403 Forbidden response; the team remains.
Ordinary members of the team cannot delete it and receive a 403 Forbidden response; the team remains.
Users who are not in the team cannot delete it (403), and guests are redirected to the login page.
A personal team cannot be deleted, even by its owner; the request is refused and the team remains.
The team settings page shows a 'Delete team' section with a confirmation dialog only to the team owner and only for non-personal teams.
assumptions: Personal teams cannot be deleted, because every user must always keep a personal team (as in Laravel Jetstream).
Deletion is permanent (no soft deletes) and memberships are removed together with the team, either via cascading foreign keys or explicitly in the action.
Members affected by the deletion are not emailed; no notification is sent.
The owner confirms in a dialog by clicking a button; re-entering the team name or password is not required.

The route teams.destroy is added to routes/settings.php next to the existing team settings routes, behind the auth and verified middleware, and after deletion the owner is redirected to the dashboard.
Authorization is enforced through TeamPolicy::delete, which is called from a form request.
plan.understood_as: New permission and behaviour: deleting a team
plan.current_behavior: New. Teams can be created, renamed, switched between and have members removed or their roles changed, but no one can delete a team.
preserve: Everyone still has a personal team, and it can never be deleted.
Users can still switch between the teams they belong to, and their current team always points to a team they belong to.
Admins can still rename the team, change members' roles and remove members, but cannot delete the team.
Members can still see the team, but cannot change or delete it.
The owner can still do everything in the team, including renaming it and managing members.
Renaming a team and the existing team settings page keep working unchanged.
Deleting a user account (profile settings) keeps working as it does now.

review.summary: The diff adds team deletion and covers every acceptance criterion. A DELETE route named teams.destroy uses a form request that calls a new TeamPolicy::delete check. The check allows only the owner and never a personal team, and the configuration cannot override it. A transactional DeleteTeam action removes all memberships, moves everyone whose current team was the deleted team back to a team they still belong to (personal team first), and then deletes the team. The owner is redirected to the dashboard with a 'Team deleted.' success toast. The settings page shows a 'Delete team' section with a confirmation dialog only when the viewer may delete the team and it is not a personal team. New feature tests cover the owner, admins (including admins granted every permission), members, outsiders, guests, personal teams, the current-team fallback and whether the delete option shows. No tests were deleted or weakened, and all verification checks passed. Nothing under 'Must stay as it is' is changed: rename, role changes, member removal, switching teams and account deletion are untouched.

changes.behavior: Deleting a team from the team settings page
changes.now: The owner of a team that is not a personal team sees a 'Delete team' section with a warning in the team settings. After they confirm in a dialog, the team is permanently deleted, and the owner is taken to the dashboard with a 'Team deleted.' message.
Only the team's owner can delete it. Admins, ordinary members and people outside the team are refused, and the team settings cannot change this.

changes.before: Personal teams could not be deleted.
changes.now: Personal teams still cannot be deleted. They show no delete option, and a direct attempt to delete one is refused.

changes.before: Not applicable, because teams could not be deleted.
changes.now: Everyone in the deleted team loses access to it. Anyone who was working in that team, including the owner, is moved back to their personal team. People who were working in a different team stay where they are.

data.summary: The owner of a team gets a 'Delete team' option in the team settings. After they confirm, the team and its memberships are removed, and anyone who was using that team is moved back to their personal team.

data.account:
Team owners can now delete a team.

- Route: DELETE settings/teams/{team}, named teams.destroy. It sits next to teams.update in routes/settings.php, behind the auth and verified middleware.
- Authorization: new TeamPolicy::delete. It allows the request only when the user is the team's owner and the team is not a personal team. The check is called from the new form request TeamDestroyRequest. Admins, members and people outside the team get 403, and guests are redirected to the login page. Deleting is owner-only whatever config/teams.php says, and the config comment and membership notes now say so.
- Action: new App\Actions\Teams\DeleteTeam. Inside one transaction it removes all memberships, moves everyone whose current team was the deleted team to another team they belong to (their personal team first, the same rule RemoveTeamMember uses), then deletes the team. The existing foreign keys already cascade or null out on delete, so no migration was needed.
- Controller: TeamController::destroy runs the action, flashes the success toast 'Team deleted.' and redirects to the dashboard. The edit page now also sends a can.deleteTeam flag.
- Frontend: Team.vue has a 'Delete team' danger section with a confirm/cancel dialog, modelled on DeleteUser.vue. It shows only when can.deleteTeam is true and the team is not personal. I regenerated the Wayfinder helpers.
- Tests: new tests/Feature/Teams/DeleteTeamTest.php (9 tests). It covers an owner deleting a team (team and memberships gone, redirect, flash), current teams being switched for the owner and members, 403 for admins (also when admins are given every permission in config), members and outsiders, guests redirected to login, a personal team that cannot be deleted, and the page flag.
- Notes: updated .builder/capabilities/teams.md (new rule, 'Delete a team' behaviour, paths) and membership.md.

Checks: pint --test passed. phpstan passed with 0 errors. php artisan test passed (74 tests). npm run check (format and lint) passed....

findings.summary: The overall verification status is reported as 'unverified', even though every individual step passed and protected acceptance tests were not applicable. Nothing failed, but the change has no protected acceptance test run behind it.

The fallback team is chosen with orderByDesc('personal_team'), which assumes the column orders so that true comes first. That holds for a PostgreSQL boolean. A user with no remaining teams would get a null current team, which should not happen because everyone has a personal team.

The capability notes now say role permissions are set in one place 'except deleting a team', which records a deliberate exception to the config-driven permission rule. This is reasonable, but the owner should know that team deletion cannot be granted to admins through configuration.

TeamDestroyRequest has an empty rules() array. A plain $this->authorize('delete', $team) in the controller would do the same job, but a form request matches the sibling TeamUpdateRequest, so this is acceptable.
